articles.title: Colien House by Alvaro Siza
articles.summary: The compact house is organized around the site slope and vegetation. A descending volume responds to topography and access conditions.

articles.title: Semibreve Studio by Clara Nahas
articles.summary: The studio uses rigorous zoning and an inverted spatial flow. A 55-square-meter plan reverses conventional public and private hierarchy.

articles.title: Basque Museum Bilbao renovation
articles.summary: Vallillo and Architects won a competition for the museum renovation. The project covers architectural and museographic rehabilitation.

articles.title: Veja São Paulo Store / Roberto Somlo Arquitetura
articles.summary: The project transforms an existing building on Oscar Freire Street, in the Jardim Paulista neighborhood, to house the first VEJA store in Brazil. The store is a radical encounter between exposed history and São Paulo modernism.

articles.title: CitySquash / Gluck+
articles.summary: CitySquash is a not-for-profit after-school enrichment program serving youth in the Bronx and Brooklyn through an integrated model of athletics, academics and mentorship. As the organization expanded beyond its existing scattered facilities serving more than 225 students annually, a new center was designed within the neighborhood it already serves, bringing these services together into a cohesive whole.

articles.title: Success Academy Bronx K–12 Campus / SOM
articles.summary: Success Academy (SA)—one of the nation's largest and highest-performing public charter networks—educates 22,000 students, primarily from low-income backgrounds, across 60 New York City schools. Founded on the belief that all children can excel when given access to exceptional teaching and learning environments, SA is nationally recognized for its rigorous academics, robust arts and athletics programming, and deep focus on college preparedness. articles.title: Lele Hotel / The Lab Evn
articles.summary: Located in Vayots Dzor, Lele Hotel is conceived as a direct response to the character and topography of its mountainous surroundings. Rather than imposing a separate architectural object on the landscape, the design seeks continuity with the terrain through its materiality, proportions, and relationship to the existing slope.

articles.summary: These bottles are by Taiwanese industrial designer Rock Wang and design firm Agoood . They were designed for Hosay , a Taiwanese brand of sustainable cleaning and bodycare products. Embodying their mission, Wang and Agoood's clever design incorporates a funnel, easing refilling: Upon embarking on the project, these are the questions the design team asked themselves: Could the cap double as a funnel? articles.title: A Spherical Computer Monitor Pays Homage to a 1970 JVC Design
articles.summary: In 1969, the world saw images of the Apollo 11 mission to the moon. In 1970 Japanese consumer electronics company JVC, presumably inspired by the Apollo 11 crew's helmets, released this: That's the Videosphere, a CRT television. It was offered with both a plain base and an alarm clock option. It's not actually attached to the base, by the way. Rather, it sits in a hemispherical depression. It came with that chain that you see, as it could also be ceiling-hung. articles.summary: The oceanfront home centers around a substantial brick chimney. The design gives the house a grounded heart. It was completed in 1984.

articles.title: Hidden Mechanism Turns Scissor Chair Into Lounger
articles.summary: A scissor chair can transform into a lounger through a hidden mechanism. The design separates seating and relaxation choices. It offers a clever furniture solution.

articles.title: Japanese Guitar Scissors Come With Mini Stand
articles.summary: The guitar scissors are made in Japan and include a mini stand. They are cute and unique stationery. They add a playful accessory for musicians.

articles.title: Touchscreen Device Woven Into Sleeves
articles.summary: Future touchscreen devices may be woven into clothing sleeves. The concept integrates controls into wearable fabric. It moves away from plastic device designs.

articles.title: Mori Mushroom Robot Offers Company Without Words
articles.summary: Mori is a mushroom-shaped robot with glowing eyes. It offers companionship without speaking. OKA designed it as an approachable nightstand companion.

articles.title: 3D-Printed Lamps Shape Light With Mazes
articles.summary: Five 3D-printed lamps use mazes and moving rings to shape light. The designs blend technology and craftsmanship. They explore new lighting possibilities.

articles.title: Bandit9 Motorcycle Fades From Red to Aluminum
articles.summary: The custom Bandit9 motorcycle changes from racing red to brushed aluminum. It is an avant-garde custom motorcycle design. The Vietnam studio created it.

articles.title: AYN Odin 3 Portal Handheld Has Sculpted Grips
articles.summary: The AYN Odin 3 Portal handheld pairs a flat glass front with sculpted grips. It aims to be comfortable for gaming. The design addresses handheld ergonomics.

articles.title: Teenage Engineering EP-35 Amp Has Hidden Cable Compartment
articles.summary: The EP-35 amp opens to reveal a hidden cable compartment. The feature keeps accessories organized. It is a simple unglamorous design detail.

articles.title: Best Audio Designs for Owning Music
articles.summary: The list highlights audio designs for people who want to own music. It considers albums as folders, discs, or cassettes. The focus is on personal audio systems.

articles.title: FilaLoom Weaves Yarn Into 3D Prints
articles.summary: FilaLoom weaves yarn into 3D printed objects. No extra motors are needed for the mechanism. The result has a basketlike texture.

articles.title: Gubi Revives Carlo Nason's Lotus Table Lamp
articles.summary: Gubi revives Carlo Nason's cult-favorite Lotus table lamp. The sculptural glass lamp returns with a subtle update. Originally introduced in 1969, it remains a design icon.

articles.title: Grace Zhang's Art Draws on Light, Finance, Chanel
articles.summary: Grace Zhang is a San Francisco-based artist. Her work explores unexpected connections between science, finance, and fashion. A recent Friday Five highlights her inspirations and paintings.

articles.title: Apparatus Explores Persian Mythology in Act V
articles.summary: Apparatus presents Act V: Afsaneh. Designer Gabriel Hendifar draws on Persian heritage and personal history. The collection explores creation, transformation, and renewal.

articles.title: Sakamoto's Kinetic Thread Column Creates Shifting Shadows
articles.summary: Yotaro Sakamoto created a kinetic thread column. Fine threads form a delicate column that moves with nearby visitors. It casts constantly changing shadows.

articles.title: Dezeen Unveils Updated Website
articles.summary: Dezeen unveiled an updated website with a new look and feel developed with creative technology studio Made by On. The refreshed site is richer, more versatile, and reflects the current direction of Dezeen.

articles.title: Adrian Smith Gordon Gill Unveils Lilli
articles.summary: US architecture firm Adrian Smith + Gordon Gill has revealed a slender residential skyscraper, called Lilli, for Miami's waterfront. Designed for quiet refinement, the development marks their latest project in the city.

articles.title: Loader Monteith Expands Red Brick Bungalow
articles.summary: A Scottish architecture studio transformed a two-bedroom red-brick bungalow into a four-bedroom family home in Prestwich, Manchester. The project successfully added square meters in a remarkably compact footprint.

articles.title: Foster Partners Designs Skyscrapers in Yerevan
articles.summary: British studio Foster + Partners will build World Trade Center Yerevan featuring two skyscrapers joined by three garden bridge elements. One tower will house offices while the other contains apartments.

articles.title: EZVIZ Smart Entry Wins Dual Awards
articles.summary: EZVIZ's Smart Entry Solutions have won consecutive international awards, including the European Product Design Award and the Golden Pin Design Award. This indicates a shift from traditional home security to prioritizing living enjoyment.

articles.title: Bobcat Earns Second Red Dot Award
articles.summary: Bobcat received a second Red Dot Award for its RogueX3 machine. The recognition highlights its Breakthrough Machine Architecture.

articles.title: Garage as Showroom Reshapes Vehicle Bays
articles.summary: An article discusses how industrial design is transforming modern vehicle service bays into interactive showrooms. This shift brings innovation to traditional auto repair environments.

articles.title: MacBook Pro Upgrade Faces Problem Ahead
articles.summary: Next week's upcoming MacBook Pro could feature a huge upgrade, though a significant flaw remains. Users anticipate major improvements, but a critical issue might hinder performance.

articles.title: TU/e Celebrates 25 Years Industrial Design
articles.summary: Eindhoven University of Technology is marking 25 years of its Industrial Design program at Dutch Design Week. The celebration focuses on designs aimed at making the world a better place.

articles.title: Exhibition on Britain's First Industrial Designer
articles.summary: An exhibition exploring Christopher Dresser, widely regarded as Britain's first industrial designer, has been announced. The retrospective highlights his pioneering contributions to early industrial design.
